 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 19.10.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.149/2016 ON THE FILE OF C/C II ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL JMFC, AND ADDITIONAL MACT,
CHITRADURGA, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.2,84,700/-
WITH INTEREST @ 9% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL REALIZATION AND ETC.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT

In this appeal, The Insurance Company is challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 19.10.2017 in MVC No.149/2016 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T-V, Chitradurga (the 'Tribunal' for short).
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T-V, Chitradurga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are, on 10.10.2015 at about 9.30 a.m., while the petitioner was riding the NC: 2024:KHC:37534 motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA-41/EB-8990 near Nagaraja Glass and Plywood, main post office road at Chitradurga, another motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA-16/M-6821 (for short 'the offending motor cycle') dashed against this motor cycle, due to which he sustained the injuries to his hands.

After taking treatment at Basaveshwara Hosptital,
Chitradurga, he went home for rest.
After 43 days, he filed the complaint with the Police and thereafter approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company and the owner of the motor cycle remained ex-parte.

The Tribunal after taking evidence and hearing both the parties, awarded compensation of Rs.2,84,700/- with interest at 9% per annum, directing the owner and the insurer of the offending motor cycle to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company is before this Court.

sentences.text:
Heard the argument of Sri. D. Vijayakumar, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Sri.
R. Shashidhar, leaned counsel for the petitioner.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that, the petitioner has suffered injuries to left hand and he was admitted to Basaveshwara Hospital on 10.10.2015.
He was under hospitalization till 19.10.2015 for a period of 9 days.
Whereas the complaint was filed to the Police on 23.11.2015 after 44 days of delay.
There is no explanation for delay offered by the petitioner.

6. It is further contended that the offending motor cycle is not involved in the accident, 44 days after the accident, there was a collusion between the petitioner, police and the Advocate representing the petitioner in creating a false theory for the sake of compensation.

Referring to the cross-examination of the petitioner it is argued that the petitioner is a degree holder, complaint was drafted by his advocate, NC: 2024:KHC:37534 till 23.11.2015 no MLC was registered by the police, whereas self-fall has been tempered as RTA in collusion with the Medical Officer also.
The petitioner by filing an affidavit did not registered the MLC and the MLC was received by the police only on 23.11.2015.
If really the petitioner has taken treatment on 10.10.2015 having met with an accident involving the two motor cycles, he ought to have informed the same in the hospital.
Only in the OPD card there is a reference of hit by bike on 10.10.2015 at around 9.30 a.m. and in the case sheet the history has been furnished as "alleged h/o RTA around 9.30 a.m. on 10.10.2015."
Fraud has been played, police records have been built up and the claim petition is presented for the sake of compensation.

This kind of fraud cannot be supported and the claim petition is required to be dismissed with exemplory cost against the petitioner and a legal action has to be initiated against the advocate who was involved in such kind of a fraud.
NC: 2024:KHC:37534 7.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that on 13.10.2015 in the MLC extract there is a specific reference to the history of RTA.
The petitioner has not suppressed factum of accident before the Medical Officer.
After the discharge, the petitioner has gone to the village for taking rest and for this reason there was a delay in filing the complaint.
The owner of the vehicle has promised the petitioner to reimburse the medical expenses but he became silent later and for these reasons, the petitioner is constrained to file the complaint.
The Tribunal has rightly appreciated the entire evidence on record and found that there is no collusion or fraud played and assessed the compensation and he has supported the impugned judgment.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.

sentences.text: 3 9. It is pertinent to note that there are two complaints that are placed before the Tribunal as Exs.P.1 and P.7.
Ex . P.7
is the complaint filed to the police on 23.11.2015.
Ex.P.2 is the FIR, which was registered on 24.11.2015 at 7.30 p.m.

There is no reference of Ex.P.7 complaint in the FIR, but a separate complaint is prepared as per Ex.P.1, narrating the detailed story from 10.10.2015 to 24.11.2015, incorporating the name of the 1st respondent as the owner of the motor cycle, that he has promised the petitioner to reimburse the treatment expenses but did not come forward.
On the basis of law is set into motion, Investigating Officer ceased the motor cycle in question, inspected the spot on 25.11.2015 and thereafter filed the charge sheet on 30.12.2015.
The delay in filing the complaint itself is 44 days, the Investigating Officer has investigated the case in rocket speed and presented the charge sheet against the rider of the offending motor cycle.
Interesting to note that the owner of the motor cycle is placed NC: 2024:KHC:37534 exparte before the Tribunal as well as in this appeal.
This clearly goes to show that the owner of the offending motor cycle is watching the proceedings from outside the Court.
10. When an accident had taken place, immediately injured person goes to the hospital, who informs the history of the accident to the casualty medical officer who treats him in hospital.
The case sheet is made available from the Basaveshwara Hospital.
OPD card is also made available with a seal of MLC.
The history mentioned is "H/O hit by bike on 10.10.2015 at around 9.30 a.m."
The OPD card did not point out the nature of vehicle, rider of the offending bike and its registration number.
Same is the recitals in discharge summary also.
11. PW-2/Dr.Ambrish, orthopedic surgeon of the Basaveshwara Medical College Hospital, the treated doctor, whose testimony shows that the petitioner was treated in his hospital as a Non-MLC case.
MLC was NC: 2024:KHC:37534 registered only after the petitioner filed an affidavit to him requesting recording the MLC.
Inpatient records, refers date as 13.10.2015, MLC was registered.
It is interesting to note that no such MLC intimation was either sent or received by the police at all.
Only after the petitioner files the complaint to the police under Ex.P.7.
On 23.11.2015, MLC intimation was received by the Police.

It goes to show that the petitioner after filing the affidavit to the PW-2,
got registered the MLC and carried the intimation to the police on 23.11.2015.
The Investigating Officer in spite of receiving Ex.P.7 complaint, he did not register the FIR.
Only on 24.11.2015 at 7.30 p.m., the FIR came to be registered on the basis of the Ex.P.1 complaint.
This clearly goes to show that from the beginning, till the filing of Ex.P.1 complaint, some filters have been used by the petitioner.

12. The cross-examination of the petitioner has demonstrated that the advocate who represented him - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:37534 in the claim petition was drafted Ex.P.1 complaint, PW-1 attested it on 23.11.2015.

According to petitioner after discharge on 19.10.2015, he went to the village, after 44 days he returns and goes to the advocate, medical officer records MLC, advocate drafts the complaint, he carries it to the police station to register the FIR.

Accordingly, the intervention of the police began on 23.11.2015 till then the truth was prevailed that the petitioner was treated as The Branch Manager vs Sri. G. R. Shyamsundar on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83917772/
4 non-MLC patient.
13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The evidence of the PW-2/Dr. Ambrish, played very important role, that in the course of cross- examination he has specifically asserted that whenever he receives a patient for treatment who sustained injuries in road traffic accident, he used to record the MLC and intimate the police.
In this case, he has not registered any MLC nor sent any police intimation.
MLC was registered only after receipt of the affidavit of the petitioner.

This clearly goes to show that the petitioner - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:37534 has taken treatment as a non-MLC case in the hospital, but later due to the involvement of others he wants to convert the non-MLC into MLC and the reason is well known that it was for the purpose of getting compensation.
14.
The petitioner has not explained how he came to know the details of offending motor cycle.

On 23.11.2015, the Investigating Officer keeps silent and sits on Ex.P.7 and acts only on Ex.P.1 on 24.11.2015 to register the FIR, thereafter he completes the formality of investigation and files the charge sheet.

The Investigating Officer has not entered the witness box explaining the circumstances and why the MLC intimation sent from Basaveshwara Medical College Hospital on 13.10.2015 was received by him 23.11.2015, where the hospital as well as the Police Station are located within stone-throwing distance.
These are the aspect that clearly point out that the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:37534 fraud has been played to facilitate the petitioner to make bonanza.

15. The Division Bench of this court in Veerappa and Another vs. Siddappa and Another1, discusses and details about this kind of case where the fraud has been played, evidence and the allegations made in the claim petition cannot be accepted as a gospel of truth.

entities.text: Veerappa and Another vs. Siddappa and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Division Bench also held that the proof of facts required to be explained satisfactorily, when the fraud is established from the materials on record, there is no question of fastening the liability against the Insurance Company.

Since the owner of the vehicle is hand in glove with the petitioner, he has to compensate the petitioner.
16.
Identical is the facts of this case.

Hence, applying the principle laid down in the said case, it is a fit case rather than dismissing the claim petition in its entirety, to direct the petitioner to go against the ILR 2009 KAR 3562 - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:37534 owner of the offending motor cycle and recover the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal.

The Branch Manager vs Sri. G. R. Shyamsundar on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83917772/
5 17.

entities.text: Branch Manager vs Sri. G. R. Shyamsundar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On careful perusal of the impugned judgment, it is pertinent to note that the Tribunal did not consider the fraud aspect of the case.
It has simply proceeded that it is a genuine case and assessed the compensation Tribunal loss sight of the fraud, which is emanating on the face of the record.
It is erroneous on the part of the Tribunal to entertain such claim petition, which ought to have been nipped at the bud.
The petitioner cannot be permitted to make a windfall of bonanza on the guise of injury sustained by him in an accident not involving the motor cycle in question.

SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE BKN
